units.zh: 宗室
units.en: The Imperial Clan
units.literal: Imperial Clan

units.zh: 〈（案：《晉宗室列傳》，《永樂大典》僅存四篇，余多殘闕。）〉
units.en: (Note: The biographies of the Jin imperial clan in the Yongle Encyclopedia survive in only four sections; most of the rest is defective or missing.)〉
units.literal: (Note: The biographies of the Jin imperial clan in the Yongle Encyclopedia survive in only four sections; the remainder is largely defective or missing.)〉

units.zh: 廣王敬威，字奉信，高祖之從父弟也。
units.en: Prince Jingwei of Guang, styled Fengxin, was Gaozu's younger paternal cousin.
units.literal: Prince of Guang Jingwei, styled Fengxin, was a younger cousin of Gaozu on the paternal side.

units.zh: 父萬詮，贈太尉，追封趙王。
units.en: His father Wanquan was posthumously honored as Grand Commandant and enfeoffed as Prince of Zhao.
units.literal: His father Wanquan was posthumously conferred Grand Commandant and enfeoffed as Prince of Zhao.

units.zh: 敬威少善騎射，事後唐莊宗，以從戰有功，累歷軍職。
units.en: From youth Jingwei excelled at horsemanship and archery. He served Later Tang's Emperor Zhuangzong and, for his service in battle, rose through a series of military posts.
units.literal: From youth Jingwei was skilled in horsemanship and archery; he served Later Tang's Emperor Zhuangzong and, for merit in following campaigns, rose through successive military posts.

units.zh: 明宗即位，擢為奉聖指揮使。
units.en: When Emperor Mingzong came to the throne, Jingwei was promoted to commander of the Fengsheng Guard.
units.literal: When Emperor Mingzong took the throne, he was promoted to commander of the Fengsheng Guard.

units.zh: 天成、應順中，凡十改軍額，累官至檢校工部尚書，賜忠順保義功臣。
units.en: During the Tiancheng and Yingshun eras he changed army designations ten times in all, rose to Acting Minister of Works, and was granted the title of Meritorious Minister, Loyal and Obedient, Protector of Righteousness.
units.literal: During the Tiancheng and Yingshun eras he changed army designations ten times in all, rose to Acting Minister of Works, and was granted the title Meritorious Minister Loyal and Obedient, Protector of Righteousness.

units.zh: 清泰中，加兵部尚書、彰聖都指揮使，遙領常州刺史。
units.en: In the Qingtai era he was further made Minister of War and commander-in-chief of the Zhangsheng Army, and held the prefecture of Changzhou in absentia.
units.literal: In the Qingtai era he was further made Minister of War and commander-in-chief of the Zhangsheng Army, and held the post of prefect of Changzhou in absentia.

units.zh: 及高祖建義於太原，敬威時在洛下，知禍必及，召所親謂曰：「夫人生而有死，理之常也。
units.en: When Gaozu raised his righteous enterprise at Taiyuan, Jingwei was in Luoyang. Seeing that disaster was inevitable, he summoned his intimates and said, "That we are born only to die is the constant way of things.
units.literal: When Gaozu raised his righteous enterprise at Taiyuan, Jingwei was then in Luoyang. Knowing that disaster was inevitable, he summoned his intimates and said, "That man is born to die is the constant principle of nature.

units.zh: 我兄方圖大舉，餘固不可偷生待辱，取笑一時。」
units.en: My elder brother is planning a great undertaking; I surely cannot cling to life and await disgrace, becoming a laughingstock to the age."
units.literal: My elder brother is planning a great undertaking; as for me, I surely cannot cling to life and await disgrace, becoming a laughingstock for the age."

units.zh: 乃自殺於私邸，人甚壯之。
units.en: He then took his own life in his private residence, and people greatly admired his courage.
units.literal: He then killed himself in his private residence, and people greatly admired his conduct.

units.zh: 天福二年，冊贈太傅，葬於河南縣。
units.en: In Tianfu 2 he was posthumously enfeoffed by edict as Grand Tutor and buried in Henan County.
units.literal: In the second year of Tianfu he was posthumously enfeoffed by edict as Grand Tutor and buried in Henan County.

units.zh: 六年，追封廣王。
units.en: In the sixth year he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Guang.
units.literal: In the sixth year he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Guang.

units.zh: 子訓嗣，官至左武衛將軍。
units.en: His son Xun succeeded him and rose to general of the Left Martial Guard.
units.literal: His son Xun succeeded him and rose to general of the Left Martial Guard.

units.zh: 敬威弟赟。
units.en: Jingwei's younger brother Yun.
units.literal: Jingwei's younger brother Yun.

units.zh: 赟，字德和，
units.en: Yun, styled Dehe,
units.literal: Yun, styled Dehe,

units.zh: （案：以下有闕文。）
units.en: (Note: text is defective below.)
units.literal: (Note: text is defective below.)

units.zh: 為陜州節度使。
units.en: He was military commissioner of Shanzhou.
units.literal: He was military commissioner of Shanzhou.

units.zh: 少帝即位，加同平章事。
units.en: When Emperor Shaodi took the throne, he was made concurrent grand councilor.
units.literal: When Emperor Shaodi took the throne, he was made concurrent Grand Councilor.

units.zh: 赟性驕慢，每使者至，必問曰：「小侄安否？」
units.en: Yun was arrogant and insolent. Whenever an envoy arrived, he invariably asked, "Is my little nephew well?"
units.literal: Yun was arrogant and insolent. Whenever an envoy arrived, he invariably asked, "Is my little nephew well?"

units.zh: 恣為暴虐，陜人苦之。
units.en: He indulged in cruelty and violence, and the people of Shan suffered under him.
units.literal: He indulged in cruelty and violence, and the people of Shan suffered under him.

units.zh: （案：以下闕。
units.en: (Note: text is defective below.
units.literal: (Note: text is defective below.

units.zh: 《少帝紀》：開運三年十二月，前曹州節度使石赟死，帝之堂叔也。
units.en: The Annals of the Young Emperor: in the twelfth month of Kaiyun 3, former Cao military commissioner Shi Yun died; he was the emperor's paternal uncle.
units.literal: The Annals of the Young Emperor: in the twelfth month of Kaiyun 3, the former military commissioner of Cao, Shi Yun, died; he was the emperor's paternal uncle.

units.zh: 《歐陽史》作墮沙壕溺死。）
units.en: The Ouyang History says he fell into a moat and drowned.)
units.literal: The Ouyang History says he fell into a moat and drowned.)

units.zh: 韓王暉，字德昭，睿祖孝平皇帝之孫，高祖之從兄也。
units.en: Prince Hui of Han, styled Dezhao, was a grandson of the Exalted Ancestor Emperor Xiaoping and Gaozu's paternal cousin.
units.literal: Prince of Han Hui, styled Dezhao, was a grandson of the Exalted Ancestor Emperor Xiaoping of filial piety and peace and a paternal cousin of Gaozu.

units.zh: 父萬友，追封秦王。
units.en: His father Wanyou was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Qin.
units.literal: His father Wanyou was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Qin.

units.zh: 暉生而龐厚，剛毅雄直，有器局，行不由徑，臨事多智，故高祖於宗族之中，獨厚遇之。
units.en: Hui was born stout and solid, firm, bold, and upright, with breadth of character. He would not take shortcuts, and in affairs he was often resourceful. Among the clan Gaozu singled him out for generous treatment.
units.literal: Hui was born stout and solid, firm and bold, upright and heroic, possessing breadth of capacity; he would not take shortcuts in his conduct, and in handling affairs he was often resourceful. Therefore among the clan Gaozu singled him out for generous treatment.

units.zh: 初，張敬達之圍晉陽也，高祖署暉為突騎都將，常引所部，出敵之不意，深入力戰，雖夷傷流血，矢鏃貫骨，而辭氣益厲，高祖壯之。
units.en: Earlier, when Zhang Jingda besieged Jinyang, Gaozu appointed Hui commander of the assault cavalry. He often led his men where the enemy did not expect, plunging deep and fighting with all his strength. Though wounded and bleeding, with arrowheads driven through bone, his voice only grew fiercer, and Gaozu admired him.
units.literal: Earlier, when Zhang Jingda besieged Jinyang, Gaozu appointed Hui commander of the assault cavalry. He would often lead his troops to strike where the enemy did not expect, plunging deep and fighting with all his strength. Though he suffered wounds and bloodshed, with arrowheads piercing bone, his tone only grew fiercer, and Gaozu admired him.

units.zh: 天福二年，遙授濠州刺史，充皇城都部署。
units.en: In Tianfu 2 he was appointed in absentia prefect of Hao and served as commander of the Imperial City garrison.
units.literal: In the second year of Tianfu he was appointed in absentia as prefect of Hao Province and served as commander of the Imperial City garrison.

units.zh: 四年，加檢校司徒，授曹州防禦使，加檢校太保。
units.en: In the fourth year he was made Acting Grand Master and appointed defender of Cao, then further made Acting Supreme Commander.
units.literal: In the fourth year he was made Acting Grand Master and appointed defender of Cao Prefecture, then further made Acting Supreme Commander.

units.zh: 其蒞任也，廉愛恤下，不營財利，不好伎樂，部人安之。
units.en: In office he was frugal and caring toward his subordinates, sought no profit, and had no taste for music or performers. The people of his command lived at ease under him.
units.literal: When he took up his post, he was frugal and loving toward his subordinates, did not pursue profit, and had no taste for music and performers. The people of his command were at peace under him.

units.zh: 歲餘，以疾終於官，歸葬太原。
units.en: After more than a year he died of illness in office and was buried at Taiyuan.
units.literal: After more than a year he died of illness in office, and his remains were buried at Taiyuan.

units.zh: 八年，冊贈太師，追封韓王。
units.en: In the eighth year he was posthumously enfeoffed by edict as Grand Preceptor and as Prince of Han.
units.literal: In the eighth year he was posthumously enfeoffed by edict as Grand Preceptor and enfeoffed as Prince of Han.

units.zh: 子曦嗣。
units.en: His son Xi succeeded him.
units.literal: His son Xi succeeded him.

units.zh: （《宋史·石曦傳》：天福中，以曦為右神武將軍歷漢至周，為右武衛、左神武二將軍。
units.en: (The Song History, Biography of Shi Xi: during Tianfu he served as general of the Right Divine Martial Guard, continuing through Han into Zhou as general of the Right Martial Guard and the Left Divine Martial Guard.
units.literal: (The Song History, Biography of Shi Xi: during Tianfu, Xi was appointed general of the Right Divine Martial Guard, continuing through Han into Zhou as general of the Right Martial Guard and the Left Divine Martial Guard.

units.zh: 恭帝即位，初為左衛將軍，會高麗王昭加恩，命曦副左驍衛將軍戴交充使。
units.en: When Emperor Gongdi took the throne, he was first made general of the Left Guard. When the king of Goryeo, Zhao, received imperial favor, Xi was ordered to serve as deputy to Dai Jiao, general of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guard, on an embassy.
units.literal: When Emperor Gongdi took the throne, he was first made general of the Left Guard. When the king of Goryeo, Zhao, received imperial favor, Xi was ordered to serve as deputy to Dai Jiao, general of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guard, as envoy.

units.zh: 淳化四年卒。）
units.en: He died in Chunhua 4.)
units.literal: He died in the fourth year of Chunhua.)

units.zh: 剡王重胤。
units.en: Prince Chongyin of Shan.
units.literal: Prince of Shan Chongyin.

units.zh: 〈（案：郯王以下諸王傳，《永樂大典》原闕。
units.en: (Note: The biographies of the princes from Prince of Tan downward were originally missing from the Yongle Encyclopedia.
units.literal: (Note: The biographies of the princes from Prince of Tan downward were originally missing from the Yongle Encyclopedia.

units.zh: 《歐陽史》云：重允，高祖弟也，亦不知其為親疏，然高祖愛之，養以為子，故於名加「重」而下齒諸子。
units.en: The Ouyang History says Chongyun was Gaozu's younger brother; whether he was close or distant kin is unknown, yet Gaozu loved him and raised him as a son. Therefore "Chong" was added to his name and he was ranked below Gaozu's sons.
units.literal: The Ouyang History says Chongyun was Gaozu's younger brother; it is also unknown whether he was close or distant kin, yet Gaozu loved him and raised him as a son. Therefore the character "Chong" was added to his name and he was ranked below the sons.

units.zh: 《通鑒·齊王紀》：高帝少弟重胤早卒。）〉
units.en: The Comprehensive Mirror, Annals of the Prince of Qi: Gaozu's youngest brother Chongyin died young.)〉
units.literal: The Comprehensive Mirror, Annals of Prince of Qi: Gaozu's youngest brother Chongyin died young.)〉

units.zh: 虢王重英。
units.en: Prince Chongying of Guo.
units.literal: Prince of Guo Chongying.

units.zh: 〈（案：《虢王傳》，《永樂大典》原闕。
units.en: (Note: The biography of the Prince of Guo was originally missing from the Yongle Encyclopedia.
units.literal: (Note: The biography of Prince of Guo was originally missing from the Yongle Encyclopedia.

units.zh: 考《五代會要》云：重英，高祖長子，天福四年四月追封。
units.en: The Institutions of the Five Dynasties records that Chongying was Gaozu's eldest son, posthumously enfeoffed in the fourth month of Tianfu 4.
units.literal: Examination of the Institutions of the Five Dynasties shows: Chongying was Gaozu's eldest son, posthumously enfeoffed in the fourth month of Tianfu 4.

units.zh: 是書《唐紀》：清泰三年七月己丑，誅右衛上將軍石重英。）〉
units.en: This work's Tang Annals: on jichou, the seventh month of Qingtai 3, Right Guards general Shi Chongying was executed.)〉
units.literal: This work's Tang Annals: on jichou day in the seventh month of Qingtai 3, the Right Guards general Shi Chongying was executed.)〉

units.zh: 楚王重信，字守孚，高祖第二子，後唐明宗之外孫也。
units.en: Prince Chongxin of Chu, styled Shoufu, was Gaozu's second son and a maternal grandson of Later Tang's Emperor Mingzong.
units.literal: Prince of Chu Chongxin, styled Shoufu, was Gaozu's second son and a maternal grandson of Later Tang's Emperor Mingzong.

units.zh: 少敏悟，有智思。
units.en: From youth he was keen and perceptive, with a thoughtful mind.
units.literal: From youth he was keen and perceptive, with thoughtful intelligence.

units.zh: 天成中，始授銀青光祿大夫、檢校左散騎常侍，俄加檢校刑部尚書，守相州長史。
units.en: During Tiancheng he was first made Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Glorious Culture and Acting Left Gentleman for Leisurely Correspondence, then soon Acting Minister of Justice and chief administrator of Xiang.
units.literal: During Tiancheng he was first given the titles Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Glorious Culture and Acting Left Gentleman for Leisurely Correspondence, then soon made Acting Minister of Justice and commander as chief of Xiang Prefecture.

units.zh: 未幾，遷金紫光祿大夫，超拜檢校司徒，守左金吾衛大將軍。
units.en: Before long he was made Grand Master of Golden-gleaming Purple Purpose and promoted in one step to Acting Grand Master, commanding as general of the Left Golden Crow Guard.
units.literal: Before long he was transferred to Grand Master of Golden-gleaming Purple Purpose and promoted in one step to Acting Grand Master, commanding as general of the Left Golden Crow Guard.

units.zh: 重信歷事唐明宗及閔帝、末帝，不恃貴戚，能克己復禮，常恂恂如也，甚為時論所稱。
units.en: Chongxin served Emperors Mingzong, Min, and Mo of Tang. He did not trade on his noble kinship; he could restrain himself and return to propriety, always earnest and deferential, and won high praise from his contemporaries.
units.literal: Chongxin served through Emperor Mingzong and Emperors Min and Mo of Tang. He did not rely on his noble kinship; he could restrain himself and return to propriety, always earnest and deferential. Contemporary opinion praised him highly.

units.zh: 高祖即位，出鎮孟津，到任逾月，去民病十餘事，朝廷有詔褒之。
units.en: When Gaozu took the throne, Chongxin was sent to govern Mengjin. Within a month of taking office he removed more than ten abuses afflicting the people, and the court issued an edict commending him.
units.literal: When Gaozu took the throne, Chongxin was sent out to govern Mengjin. Within a month of taking office he removed more than ten abuses afflicting the people, and the court issued an edict commending him.

units.zh: 是歲，範延光叛命於鄴，詔遣前靈武節度使張從賓發河橋屯兵數千人，東討延光。
units.en: That year Fan Yanguang rebelled at Ye. An edict ordered the former military commissioner of Lingwu, Zhang Congbin, to mobilize several thousand troops at Heqiao and march east against Yanguang.
units.literal: That year Fan Yanguang rebelled at Ye. An edict ordered the former military commissioner of Lingwu, Zhang Congbin, to mobilize several thousand troops stationed at Heqiao and march east against Yanguang.

units.zh: 既而從賓與延光合謀為亂，遂害重信於理所，時年二十。
units.en: Before long Congbin joined Yanguang in plotting rebellion and murdered Chongxin at his headquarters. He was twenty.
units.literal: Before long Congbin joined Yanguang in plotting rebellion and thereupon murdered Chongxin at his administrative quarters. He was twenty years old.

units.zh: 遠近聞者，為之嘆惜。
units.en: All who heard of it, near and far, sighed with regret.
units.literal: Those far and near who heard of it sighed with regret.

units.zh: 詔贈太尉。
units.en: An edict posthumously honored him as Grand Commandant.
units.literal: An edict posthumously honored him as Grand Commandant.

units.zh: 時執事奏曰：「兩漢子弟，生死無歷三公位者。」
units.en: The officials at court memorialized, saying, "In the two Han dynasties, no imperial kinsman in life or death ever held one of the three top offices."
units.literal: The officials at court memorialized, saying, "In the two Han dynasties, imperial kinsmen in life or death never held the three top offices."

units.zh: 高祖曰：「此兒為善被禍，予甚湣之，自我作古，寧有例乎。」
units.en: Gaozu said, "This boy did good yet suffered disaster; I pity him deeply. To break precedent myself—what example is there?"
units.literal: Gaozu said, "This boy did good yet suffered disaster; I pity him deeply. To break precedent and establish a new rule—can there be an example?"

units.zh: 遂行冊命。
units.en: The enfeoffment ceremony was then carried out.
units.literal: The enfeoffment ceremony was then carried out.

units.zh: 以其年十月，葬河南萬安山。
units.en: In the tenth month of that year he was buried on Mount Wan'an in Henan.
units.literal: In the tenth month of that year he was buried on Mount Wan'an in Henan.

units.zh: 天福七年，追封沂王，少帝嗣位，改封楚王。
units.en: In Tianfu 7 he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Yi; when Emperor Shaodi succeeded, his title was changed to Prince of Chu.
units.literal: In the seventh year of Tianfu he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Yi; when Emperor Shaodi succeeded, his title was changed to Prince of Chu.

units.zh: 妃南陽白氏，昭信軍節度使奉進之女也。
units.en: His consort was Lady Bai of Nanyang, daughter of Fengjin, military commissioner of the Zhaoxin Army.
units.literal: His consort was Lady Bai of Nanyang, daughter of military commissioner Fengjin of the Zhaoxin Army.

units.zh: 重信有子二人，皆幼，長於公宮，及少帝北遷，不知其所終。
units.en: Chongxin had two sons, both still young and raised in the palace. When Emperor Shaodi was removed northward, their ultimate fate was unknown.
units.literal: Chongxin had two sons, both young; they were raised in the palace. When Emperor Shaodi was removed northward, their ultimate fate was unknown.

units.zh: 壽王重乂，字宏理，高祖第三子也。
units.en: Prince Chongyi of Shou, styled Hongli, was Gaozu's third son.
units.literal: Prince of Shou Chongyi, styled Hongli, was Gaozu's third son.

units.zh: 幼岐嶷，好儒書，亦通兵法，高祖素所鐘愛。
units.en: From youth he was precocious and sharp, loved Confucian books, and also understood military strategy; Gaozu had long cherished him.
units.literal: From youth he was precocious and sharp, loved Confucian books, and also understood military strategy; Gaozu had long cherished him.

units.zh: 及即位，自北京皇城使拜左驍衛大將軍。
units.en: When Gaozu took the throne, Chongyi was promoted from Beijing Imperial City commissioner to general of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guard.
units.literal: When Gaozu took the throne, Chongyi was promoted from Beijing Imperial City commissioner to general of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guard.

units.zh: 車駕幸浚郊，加檢校司空，權東都留守。
units.en: When the imperial carriage visited the Jun outskirts, he was made Acting Minister of Works and acting defender of the Eastern Capital.
units.literal: When the imperial carriage visited the Jun outskirts, he was made Acting Minister of Works and acting defender of the Eastern Capital.

units.zh: 未幾，鄴都範延光叛，朝廷遣楊光遠討之，詔前靈武節度使、洛都巡檢使張從賓發盟津屯兵赴鄴下。
units.en: Before long Fan Yanguang rebelled at Yedu. The court sent Yang Guangyuan to suppress him and ordered former Lingwu military commissioner and Luoyang patrol commissioner Zhang Congbin to mobilize troops at Mengjin and march to Ye.
units.literal: Before long Fan Yanguang rebelled at Yedu. The court sent Yang Guangyuan to suppress him and ordered the former military commissioner of Lingwu and Luoyang patrol commissioner Zhang Congbin to mobilize troops stationed at Mengjin and march to Ye.

units.zh: 會從賓密通延光，與婁繼英等先劫河橋，次亂洛邑，因害重乂於河南府，時年十九。
units.en: Congbin then secretly communicated with Yanguang. With Lou Jiying and others he first seized Heqiao Bridge, then threw Luoyang into disorder, and murdered Chongyi in Henan Prefecture. He was nineteen.
units.literal: Congbin then secretly communicated with Yanguang. With Lou Jiying and others he first seized Heqiao Bridge, then threw Luoyang into disorder, and thereupon murdered Chongyi in Henan Prefecture. He was nineteen years old.

units.zh: 從賓敗，高祖發哀於便殿，輟視朝三日，詔贈太傅。
units.en: When Congbin was defeated, Gaozu expressed mourning in the side hall, suspended court audiences for three days, and issued an edict posthumously honoring Chongyi as Grand Tutor.
units.literal: When Congbin was defeated, Gaozu expressed mourning in the side hall, suspended court audiences for three days, and issued an edict posthumously honoring Chongyi as Grand Tutor.

units.zh: 是歲冬十月，詔遣莊宅使張穎監護喪事，葬於河南府萬安山。
units.en: In the tenth winter month that year, an edict sent Zhang Ying, commissioner of the imperial estates, to supervise the funeral and bury him on Mount Wan'an in Henan Prefecture.
units.literal: In the tenth month of winter that year, an edict sent Zhang Ying, commissioner of the imperial estates, to supervise the funeral and bury him on Mount Wan'an in Henan Prefecture.

units.zh: 天福中，追封壽王。
units.en: During Tianfu he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Shou.
units.literal: During Tianfu he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Shou.

units.zh: 妃李氏，汾州刺史玘之女也。
units.en: His consort was Lady Li, daughter of Qi, prefect of Fen.
units.literal: His consort was Lady Li, daughter of Qi, prefect of Fenzhou.

units.zh: 重乂無子，妃後落發為尼，開運中，卒於京師。
units.en: Chongyi had no sons. His consort later took the tonsure as a nun; during Kaiyun she died in the capital.
units.literal: Chongyi had no sons. His consort later shaved her head and became a nun; during Kaiyun she died in the capital.

units.zh: 夔王重進。
units.en: Prince Chongjin of Kui.
units.literal: Prince of Kui Chongjin.

units.zh: 〈（《五代會要》云：重進，高祖第五子，天福七年四月追封。）〉
units.en: (The Institutions of the Five Dynasties says Chongjin was Gaozu's fifth son, posthumously enfeoffed in the fourth month of Tianfu 7.)〉
units.literal: (The Institutions of the Five Dynasties says: Chongjin was Gaozu's fifth son, posthumously enfeoffed in the fourth month of Tianfu 7.)〉

units.zh: 陳王重杲。
units.en: Prince Chonggao of Chen.
units.literal: Prince of Chen Chonggao.

units.zh: 〈（《歐陽史》：高祖少子曰馮六，未名而卒，贈太傅，追封陳王，賜名重杲。）〉
units.en: (The Ouyang History: Gaozu's youngest son was called Feng Six; he died before receiving a name, was posthumously honored as Grand Tutor, enfeoffed as Prince of Chen, and given the name Chonggao.)〉
units.literal: (The Ouyang History: Gaozu's youngest son was called Feng Six; he died before receiving a name, was posthumously honored as Grand Tutor, enfeoffed as Prince of Chen, and given the name Chonggao.)〉

units.zh: 重睿。
units.en: Chongrui.
units.literal: Chongrui.

units.zh: 〈（案《契丹國志》：高祖憂悒成疾，一旦馮道獨對，高祖命幼子重睿出拜之，又令宦者抱置道懷中，蓋欲馮道輔立之。
units.en: (Note: According to the Khitan State Chronicles, Gaozu, weighed down by worry, fell ill. One day Feng Dao had a private audience; Gaozu ordered his young son Chongrui to come forth and bow to him, and had a eunuch place the child in Dao's arms—apparently intending Feng Dao to assist in installing him as heir.
units.literal: (Note: According to the Khitan State Chronicles, Gaozu, oppressed by worry, fell ill. One day Feng Dao had a private audience; Gaozu ordered the young son Chongrui to come forth and bow to him, and had a eunuch place the child in Dao's arms—apparently intending Feng Dao to assist in installing him as heir.

units.zh: 高祖崩，道與侍衛馬步都虞候景延廣議，以國家多難，宜立長君，乃奉齊王重貴為嗣。
units.en: When Gaozu died, Dao discussed with Jing Yanguang, chief of the palace guards infantry and cavalry, that the state faced many difficulties and a mature ruler should be installed; they thereupon enthroned Prince Chonggui of Qi as successor.
units.literal: When Gaozu died, Dao discussed with the chief of palace guards infantry and cavalry Jing Yanguang that the state faced many difficulties and a mature ruler should be installed; they thereupon enthroned Prince of Qi Chonggui as successor.

units.zh: 《五代會要》：重睿，高祖第七子，許州節度使，未封王。
units.en: The Institutions of the Five Dynasties: Chongrui was Gaozu's seventh son, military commissioner of Xu, and had not yet received a princely title.
units.literal: The Institutions of the Five Dynasties: Chongrui was Gaozu's seventh son, military commissioner of Xu Province, and had not yet received a princely title.

units.zh: 《歐陽史》云：從出帝北遷，不知其所終。）〉
units.en: The Ouyang History says that when he followed the deposed emperor northward, his ultimate fate was unknown.)〉
units.literal: The Ouyang History says: when he followed the deposed emperor northward, his ultimate fate was unknown.)〉

units.zh: 延煦。
units.en: Yanxu.
units.literal: Yanxu.

units.zh: 〈（《五代會要》云：延煦，少帝長子，遙領陜西節度使。
units.en: (The Institutions of the Five Dynasties says Yanxu was Emperor Shaodi's eldest son and held in absentia the post of military commissioner of Shaanxi.
units.literal: (The Institutions of the Five Dynasties says: Yanxu was Emperor Shaodi's eldest son and held in absentia the post of military commissioner of Shaanxi.

units.zh: 《通鑒》云：趙在禮家資為諸帥之最，帝利其富，為皇子鎮寧節度使延煦娶其女，在禮自費緡錢十萬，縣官之費，數倍過之。）〉
units.en: The Comprehensive Mirror says Zhao Zaili's family wealth ranked highest among all commanders. The emperor coveted his riches and arranged a marriage between his daughter and Prince Yanxu, military commissioner of Zhenning; Zaili spent a hundred thousand strings of cash himself, while the government's expenditure was several times greater.)〉
units.literal: The Comprehensive Mirror says: Zhao Zaili's family wealth ranked highest among all commanders. The emperor coveted his riches and arranged a marriage between his daughter and Prince Yanxu, military commissioner of Zhenning; Zaili spent a hundred thousand strings of cash himself, while the government's expenditure was several times greater.)〉

units.zh: 延寶。
units.en: Yanbao.
units.literal: Yanbao.

units.zh: 〈（《五代會要》：延寶，少帝次子，遙領魯州節度使。
units.en: (The Institutions of the Five Dynasties: Yanbao was Emperor Shaodi's second son and held in absentia the post of military commissioner of Lu.
units.literal: (The Institutions of the Five Dynasties: Yanbao was Emperor Shaodi's second son and held in absentia the post of military commissioner of Lu Prefecture.

units.zh: 《通鑒》云：延煦及弟延寶皆高祖諸孫，帝養以為子。
units.en: The Comprehensive Mirror says Yanxu and his younger brother Yanbao were all Gaozu's grandsons; the emperor raised them as sons.
units.literal: The Comprehensive Mirror says: Yanxu and his younger brother Yanbao were all Gaozu's grandsons; the emperor raised them as sons.

units.zh: 《會要》引實錄亦云皆帝之從子，養以為子。
units.en: The Institutions, citing the Veritable Records, likewise says they were all the emperor's younger cousins, raised as sons.
units.literal: The Institutions citing the Veritable Records likewise says they were all the emperor's younger cousins, raised as sons.

units.zh: 《歐陽史》云：延煦等從帝北遷，後不知其所終。）〉
units.en: The Ouyang History says Yanxu and the others followed the emperor northward; afterward their ultimate fates were unknown.)〉
units.literal: The Ouyang History says: Yanxu and the others followed the emperor northward; afterward their ultimate fates were unknown.)〉

candidatePacket.instructions: Review dates, event ownership, conversions, endpoint evidence, age reckoning, omitted life dates, and active-date hints. Read all Chinese units for omissions; English is not independent evidence. Do not re-extract names or mentions. For each item identify whose event is dated and justify each endpoint. Same mother does not imply same birth year. Later allusions are not personal activity. Research or record a blocker rather than invent precision. A report cannot approve with missing checks or unresolved research.

findings.problem: A two-era source phrase was compressed into a point at the first era’s opening year.
findings.action: Replace the point date with chronology preserving both named eras without invented precision.

findings.problem: Wanquan chronology is borrowed from Jingwei’s later posthumous honors.
findings.action: Remove borrowed Wanquan attestation and hints; retain undated identity information.

findings.problem: A posthumous event for Jingwei was converted into a full-reign attestation for Gaozu.
findings.action: Remove this borrowed Gaozu attestation while preserving separately supported accession and death claims.

findings.problem: Hui’s death is sequenced after office, but the source gives no point year; AD 943 is posthumous reception.
findings.action: Replace the point death with supported one-sided/uncertain chronology and remove reception-derived hint content.

findings.problem: Xiaoping chronology is borrowed from his grandson Hui’s appointment and later honor.
findings.action: Remove borrowed Xiaoping attestation and hints unless independent evidence is added.

findings.problem: Wanyou chronology is borrowed from his son Hui’s appointment and later honor.
findings.action: Remove borrowed Wanyou attestation and hints unless independent evidence is added.

findings.problem: Chongyin’s early death is undated; the Gaozu-reign interval is inferred from relationship language.
findings.action: Remove interval, attestation, and hint while retaining the undated early-death statement.

findings.problem: Chongxin’s Tiancheng offices were assigned to an inferred maternal intermediary absent from the dated event.
findings.action: Remove the mother’s borrowed attestation and hint.

findings.problem: Chongxin’s Tianfu 7 title was assigned to Lady Bai and Fengjin, related people without a dated event.
findings.action: Remove both relatives’ borrowed attestations and hints.

findings.problem: Chonggao’s undated death-before-naming was given the whole Gaozu reign as personal activity.
findings.action: Remove the reign-length attestation and hint, retaining the undated death.

findings.problem: Kinship and ruler-title wording was converted into full-reign activity for four people.
findings.action: Remove all listed reign-length attestations and hints unless a personal dated event is independently documented.
